title: Capisco, leggo, dormo: i verbi in -ere e -ire
summary: Present tense of -ere and -ire verbs (including the -isc- type: capire to capisco) and yes/no questions by intonation

blocks.title: I verbi in -ere
blocks.body: The second family: **-ere** verbs. Take **leggere** (to read): *leggo, leggi, legge, leggiamo, leggete, leggono*. Same idea as -are — the ending carries the person.
blocks.callout: -ere noi/voi endings: -iamo/-ete — close to -are but with an e.

blocks.title: I verbi in -ire: due tipi
blocks.body: **-ire** verbs split into two types. Plain, like **dormire** (to sleep): *dormo, dormi, dorme, dormiamo, dormite, dormono* — same shape as -ere but with an i. But many common -ire verbs insert **-isc-** in the singular and 3rd-person plural: **capire** (to understand) becomes *capisco, capisci, capisce, capiamo, capite, capiscono*. Learn each -ire verb's type as you meet it — there's no shortcut. Bonus: to make a yes/no question, Italian **doesn't add any word** — just **raise your pitch** at the end: *Capisci l'italiano?* is a question purely by the way you say it.
blocks.callout: capire → capisco, not 'capo' — the -isc- pops in exactly where you'd hope for a shortcut.

pairs.note: Same endings, but capire-type verbs wedge -isc- into every form except noi/voi.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Io non ___ (capire) bene l'italiano al telefono.
blocks.explain: **capisco** — capire takes the -isc- insert in the io form.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the question — remember, no extra word, just the question mark shows it's a question.

blocks.scene: You run into Sofia near the university; she asks about your Italian.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.target: Ciao! Allora, capisci già un po' di italiano?
lines.en: Hi! So, do you already understand a bit of Italian?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Sì, capisco molto, ma non scrivo ancora bene.
lines.en: Yes, I understand a lot, but I don't write well yet.
lines.spotlight: scrivo — scrivere is a regular -ere verb: scrivo, scrivi, scrive.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.target: Leggi qualcosa in italiano ogni giorno?
lines.en: Do you read something in Italian every day?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Sì, leggo un po' la sera.
lines.en: Yes, I read a bit in the evening.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.target: Bravo! Dormi bene stasera, allora — domani parliamo ancora.
lines.en: Well done! Sleep well tonight then — tomorrow let's talk more.

questions.q: What does Sofia ask if 'You' does every day?

blocks.prompt: Answer for yourself, in Italian: do you understand more when reading or when listening? Write 2-3 sentences using capire, leggere, or ascoltare.
